verdicts.citation: The decisive leg is analytic and I re-derived it by hand rather than reading it. Feed that same constant to the White root: clamp(2,[-16,-1]) = -1, not -2. So NO flat tie constant reproduces the colour-symmetric (+2,-2) anchor -- the White side is pinned at -1 for every TIE >= -1 and can only reach -2 by a constant that then breaks the Black side. verdicts.citation: This is Tier C's target case -- a falsification that could wrongly kill downstream work -- and it survives every check, with a 25-day-old source line reference that still lands exactly. The claim being falsified is 'ADR-0013 Track A (memo_writes=false) escapes QA-018'. The refutation has two limbs and both hold at HEAD. (1) INDEPENDENCE OF THE TWO FLAGS, from the signature: `grep -n 'pub fn init' src/retro.zig` -> :961 `pub fn init(t: *Tables, gpa: std.mem.Allocator, budget: u64, bracketed: bool, progress_every: u64, memo_writes: bool, deps: bool) !Finisher` -- `bracketed` and `memo_writes` are two separate parameters, so turning one off says nothing about the other. (2) THE HARDCODE, at the cited line: `sed -n '2407p' src/retro.zig` -> 'var f = try RT.Finisher.init(&t, gpa, finisher_budget, true, progress_every, memo_writes, deps);' -- the fourth positional argument is `bracketed` and it is a literal `true`, while `memo_writes` is passed through from the caller. And the enclosing function is exactly the one the critique names: `grep -n '^fn ' src/retro.zig` shows the nearest preceding definition is :2331 `fn saveArtifact(comptime w: usize, comptime h: usize, ... memo_writes: bool, deps: bool, bracket_only: bool)`. So 'saveArtifact hardcodes bracketed=true (retro.zig:2407)' is literally true at HEAD, function and line. docs/epistemic/critique-2026-07-28.md:377 is the QA-019 row verbatim.
verdicts.status_should_be: FALSE -- unchanged. The row is a correct falsification of a convenient escape hatch, and correcting it would have re-opened a route that does not exist. One clarification worth adding for anyone reading the code: there are TWO finisher call sites with different behaviour -- src/retro.zig:2407 hardcodes bracketed=true, while :2522 passes the configurable `opts.finisher_bracketed` (default `true` at :2160). The artifact-saving path is the hardcoded one, which is why the shipped artifacts are all bracket-derived and why the writes-off floor inherits the premise.
